title: The German Study on Tobacco Use (4th funding period)
summary:
Smoking harms health and affects many people in Germany. The DEBRA study therefore regularly examines how many people smoke, which groups are particularly affected, and how smoking behaviour changes over time. This information helps to plan better prevention measures and support for people who want to stop smoking.
In addition to traditional cigarettes, many people today use new nicotine products such as electronic cigarettes, heated tobacco products, waterpipes and nicotine pouches. These products can carry health risks, but some people also use them to smoke less or to quit smoking. Cannabis use also plays an increasing role. The study aims to better understand how common the use of these products is, what people think and feel about them, and how they may influence tobacco control and prevention measures.
As part of the DEBRA study, around 1,500 people aged 14 to 64 years in Germany are personally interviewed at home five times per year. The results show how the use of tobacco, new nicotine products and cannabis is developing and which factors are linked to their use.
